Cayley-Dickson Algebras and Finite Geometry [![Image 3: Scispace (Formerly Typeset)](http://scispace.com/scispace-logo-square.svg)](http://scispace.com/) Sign up[Pricing](http://scispace.com/pricing?pricing_hook=header-hook) Open Access Journal Article[10.3390/MATH3041192](https://doi.org/10.3390/MATH3041192) Cayley-Dickson Algebras and Finite Geometry =========================================== [Metod Saniga,](http://scispace.com/authors/metod-saniga-3bio9v5mmh)[Frédéric Holweck,](http://scispace.com/authors/frederic-holweck-30i81bka6v)[Petr Pracna](http://scispace.com/authors/petr-pracna-41iwysgmbz) +2 more[Slovak Academy of Sciences](http://scispace.com/institutions/slovak-academy-of-sciences-2oe0ullx) -04 Dec[2015](http://scispace.com/journals/arxiv-combinatorics-11wv3snu/2015) -[arXiv: Combinatorics](http://scispace.com/journals/arxiv-combinatorics-11wv3snu) Show Less Podcast 21 [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1405.6888v2) Save Cite TL;DR: In this article, the authors show that the multiplication table of Cayley-Dickson algebras is encoded in the projective space PG$(N-1,2) of a Cayley Dickson algebra, where the imaginary units are viewed as points and distinguished triads of them as lines. Abstract:Given a 2 N-dimensional Cayley-Dickson algebra, where 3≤N≤6, we first observe that the multiplication table of its imaginary units e a, 1≤a≤2 N−1, is encoded in the properties of the projective space PG(N−1,2) if one regards these imaginary units as points and distinguished triads of them {e a,e b,e c}, 1≤a
